title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB)
summary: The Federal Reserve's Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate held steady at 3.65% on April 16, 2026, unchanged from the prior day. The rate has remained at 3.65% since at least April 12, 2026.
key_points: IORB rate: 3.65% as of 2026-04-15 (prior day comparison)
Rate has been flat at 3.65% for at least 5 consecutive observations (April 12-16, 2026)
IORB is the interest rate the Fed pays on reserve balances held by depository institutions
why_it_matters: IORB is the interest rate the Fed pays on reserve balances held by depository institutions, serving as a key administered rate in the Fed's monetary policy implementation framework. This rate influences money market rates including SOFR, repo rates, and short-term Treasury yields.
macro_context: IORB at 3.65% reflects the current policy rate floor. The source is a data snapshot and does not provide explicit commentary on monetary policy stance or the federal funds rate target range.
market_structure_context: IORB is a key administered rate in the Fed's monetary policy implementation framework. As the rate paid on excess reserves, it anchors the overnight money market and helps define the lower bound of the federal funds rate corridor.
